details.label: Summary
details.text: Damaging gusts (a couple of which may be severe) remain possible with an ongoing thunderstorm cluster over the next few hours. Storms may progress beyond the bounds of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 589, which may require a new watch issuance downstream

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A cold-pool-driven MCS continues to rapidly progress southeastward at around 45-50 kts across central and southern IN. While wind damage/gust reports have not recently been received, the MCS is preceded by 1500-3000 J/kg MLCAPE and 20-30 kts of effective bulk shear. While the deep-layer shear is relatively weak, the well-established cold pool with this MCS continues to propagate along a southward-sagging baroclinic boundary, possibly supporting tilting of modest localized horizontal vorticity in place. Assuming this is the case, it is plausible that the MCS may maintain intensity for at least a few more hours. Should this occur, the MCS will propagate past the bounds of Severe Thunderstorm Watch 589 with a damaging/severe gust threat. If this scenario becomes more apparent, a downstream Severe Thunderstorm Watch will be considered

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A cluster of storms south of the Denver Metro has produced severe gusts up to 62 mph. Mode remains fairly mixed, with multi-cell clusters and supercells ongoing across portions of eastern Colorado. The environment remains moderately unstable with around 30-35 kts of deep layer shear. Severe potential will likely increase with movement eastward into more available 60 F degree dew points. Supercells with large hail potential will continue over the next couple of hours before eventual transition to one or more linear clusters. An increase in the damaging wind threat is expected eastward into the lower Plains by the evening

details.label: Summary
details.text: The threat for severe storms capable of mainly damaging wind gusts is expected to increase across the area late this afternoon into evening. A severe thunderstorm watch is possible

details.label: Discussion
details.text: Visible satellite and surface observations indicate a couple of boundaries remnant from earlier storms located over the region as of 20Z. Objective analysis shows, and visible satellite confirms residual capping over northeast and east-central MO into adjacent west-central and southwest IL. To the south of those areas over central and southern MO, temperatures have warmed to around 100 F with considerably more boundary-layer-based cumulus development, coincident with an uncapped environment with MLCAPE of 2000-3000 J/kg. That area resides to the south of the stronger forcing for ascent and associated, stronger mid-level flow related to an MCV moving along the IA-MO border. Variability exists across the latest CAM guidance and time-lagged ensembles in specific details regarding the preferred location(s) for storm development later this afternoon. In general, there is a signal for eventual upscale growth of initial more discrete storms into an MCS, which tracks into southern IL this evening. Given the presence of a hot, well-mixed boundary layer already in place across central and southern MO, the setup appears favorable for at least isolated damaging wind gusts with the most intense storms. A more concentrated area of damaging wind potential may materialize this evening should storms merge into an MCS along a coalescing cold pool. Convective trends are being monitored for a possible watch issuance

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH
